posts.title: What an agreement in principle really tells you
posts.excerpt: An agreement in principle is a lender's first yes. It is useful, and it is also much less than most people think.
posts.content:
An agreement in principle is a lender's first yes. It is useful, and it is also much less than most people think.

To give one, a lender looks at your income, your outgoings and a soft or full credit search, and says how much it would probably lend. Estate agents like to see one because it shows that you have spoken to somebody and that your budget is real.

What it does not do

What it does not do is look at the house, read your payslips or check your deposit. Those come with the full application, and that is where most surprises happen. An agreement in principle from the wrong lender can turn into a no three weeks later.

That is why we only ask for one when we are confident the full application will follow, and why Elif checks your documents first. A quiet yes in week three is worth more than a quick yes in week one.

posts.title: Five documents to find before you call
posts.excerpt: You do not need any paperwork for a first call. You will need it soon after, and finding it early is the single best way to make a mortgage go quickly.
posts.content:
You do not need any paperwork for a first call. You will need it soon after, and finding it early is the single best way to make a mortgage go quickly.

The list

Three months of payslips, and your latest P60. Three months of bank statements for every account your salary or spending passes through. Photo ID that has not expired. Proof of where the deposit comes from: a savings statement, or a signed letter if a parent is giving you part of it. And if you are self-employed, your last two years of accounts or tax calculations.

Keep them as PDFs in one folder with plain names. Lenders read hundreds of files a week, and a tidy one is read kindly. A missing page is the most common reason for a two-week delay.

posts.title: Fixed or tracker, explained at a kitchen table
posts.excerpt: Almost every couple asks the same question at some point in the first meeting: should we fix, and for how long?
posts.content:
Almost every couple asks the same question at some point in the first meeting: should we fix, and for how long?

A fixed rate stays the same for two, three or five years, whatever happens to interest rates. You know exactly what leaves your account every month. A tracker follows the base rate up and down, usually with no penalty if you want to leave early.

We start with your budget, not with a forecast. If a payment two points higher would hurt, a fix is usually the calm choice. If you expect to move or pay off a lump sum soon, a tracker or a short fix can cost less overall. Nobody knows where rates will go, and we will never pretend to.

posts.title: Remortgaging six months early
posts.excerpt: Most fixed rates end quietly. The letter from your lender arrives a few weeks before, and if you do nothing you move onto its standard variable rate, which is usually much higher.
posts.content:
Most fixed rates end quietly. The letter from your lender arrives a few weeks before, and if you do nothing you move onto its standard variable rate, which is usually much higher.

You can usually secure a new deal up to six months before the old one ends, without paying anything to leave. If rates fall in the meantime, we can change to a cheaper product before completion. If they rise, you keep the one you secured.

So we put a note in the diary for every client and ring three months before the date at the latest. Margaret and Alan, who appear on our home page, saved a little over two hundred pounds a month by starting early.

posts.title: Self-employed with two years of accounts
posts.excerpt: Being self-employed does not make a mortgage impossible. It makes the choice of lender much more important.
posts.content:
Being self-employed does not make a mortgage impossible. It makes the choice of lender much more important.

Some lenders average your last two years. Some take the latest year if it is higher. Some will accept a single year of accounts, and some count dividends and salary together for company directors. A contractor on a day rate can often be treated almost like an employee.

Tom reads accounts all day and likes them. Before you apply, he will tell you which figure each lender will use, and which lenders to leave alone. Hannah, a joiner whose story is on our first-time buyer page, was told twice to wait a year. She did not have to.

posts.title: Thursday evenings at Linden Row
posts.excerpt: From this month the office stays open until eight every Thursday evening.
posts.content:
From this month the office stays open until eight every Thursday evening.

Many of the people we help cannot make a phone call about money at work, and do not want to spend a Saturday morning on one either. So on Thursdays Naomi or Tom will be at the round table by the window until eight, with the kettle on.

You do not need an appointment. Bring a question, a letter from your lender or a house you saw at the weekend. If it takes longer than twenty minutes, we will book a proper meeting at your kitchen table.
